Command: Beware the Leaven of the Pharisees
Summary: Jesus' warning command: beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy — the teaching that says one thing and lives another.
Commandment: Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Application: Leaven spreads quietly through the whole lump; so does hypocrisy. The command guards disciples against a religion of outward performance hiding inward corruption.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason in Luke: 'for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed' (Luke 12:2).
Function: Leaven works quietly through the whole lump, and so does hypocrisy. Not Mosaic law but a New Testament command — the threefold division does not sort it. Its goal was to guard disciples against a religion of outward performance hiding inward corruption. The evil it addressed was hypocrisy — teaching that says one thing and lives another, spreading unseen. It restrained that evil with exposure: there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed, so the hidden life cannot stay hidden forever.
